newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed after lows set, Dec ends up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed after lows set, Dec ends up.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed and trading was slow with new contract lows set early, traders said.
The new low for March was $3.74 per bushel, down from the previous low of $3.75 set Monday.
Nearby December ended higher but continued to hover in the low $3.80 per bushel level, a 16-month low for a nearby CBOT wheat futures contract.
Support came from signals the market was near-term oversold with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closing at 26.239 points.
Technicians generally consider an RSI of 30 or less a sign of an oversold market.
But long term indicators remain bearish with the key moving averages giving little encouragement to the bulls, technical traders pointed out.
Fundamentally, the market continues to get hit by competition for wheat export business from Argentina, the EU, Canada and Australia.
Wheat closed 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 3/4 lower, with December up 2-1/4 at $3.84-1/2.
Sparks Companies Monday increased to 9.6 million tonnes its estimate for 1996-97 Argentine wheat exports. In 1995-96, Argentine wheat exports totaled 4.45 million tonnes.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,000, up from 13,219 Monday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 400 March $3.60 puts and sold 400 March $4.00 puts at 22-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000, up from 5,322 Monday.
